subject.title: fix: make outbound hooks consistent for streamed replies

question: Must durable outbound queue entries written by this release remain safe when an operator rolls back to the previous release, and should the two new required plugin-runtime reply methods ship as public contract now?
rationale: Tests establish new-reader behavior, but only an owner can decide the supported rollback boundary and approve the exported plugin API expansion; those choices determine the correct persisted format and documentation.

options.title: Preserve rollback and ship the API
options.body: Retain legacy raw payloads for older readers, add a separate versioned prepared-payload representation, document the new runtime methods, and rerun exact-head upgrade and rollback proof.

options.title: Accept a one-way queue transition
options.body: Explicitly approve rollback incompatibility, define how pending entries are drained or discarded before downgrade, and document the operator procedure and plugin API change.

options.title: Keep the seam internal
options.body: Rework bundled channels through an existing internal channel-turn contract and defer the exported plugin-runtime additions until a separately reviewed compatibility proposal.

recommendation.title: Preserve rollback and ship the API
recommendation.body: Retain legacy raw payloads for older readers, add a separate versioned prepared-payload representation, document the new runtime methods, and rerun exact-head upgrade and rollback proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the proposed lifecycle implementation and have prior merged history in the central outbound path.
